transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I suppose I'm here because... I've been having a hard time with this scar on my wrist. I mean, I know it's probably not as bad as it looks to me, but... when I’m at church, or sitting down for bridge, I just keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it. It just feels like it’s the very first thing they notice about me now, and it's really been bothering me.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking or seeking reassurance about how the scar looks?

Yes, I suppose I do. Before I leave the house, I’ll usually stop at the hall mirror and check my wrist a few times. I try on different long sleeves, or maybe put on a bracelet, just to see if it covers it up well enough. And I do ask my husband about it... I'll ask him if it looks obvious. He always tells me it’s barely there, but I just need to make sure anyway.
Does this fear of being judged occur only because of your wrist scar, or does it also happen in social situations when the scar is not involved?

No, it's really just the scar. I've never been someone who worries much about what people think of me in general. I mean, I've always been perfectly fine talking to people at the office or spending time with my friends. It's just... this mark on my wrist. If it weren't for that, I wouldn't be feeling self-conscious or judged at all.
